column1: Information since September points to a still-strong labor market and moderate growth, but with muted inflation and softness in business fixed investment and exports. The 25bp cut to 1.50–1.75% and the Desk’s Treasury bill purchases/repo operations provide insurance against global headwinds and support smooth policy transmission, consistent with evidence that monetary policy influences real activity and market rates (Sims, 1992; McCallum & Nelson, 1999). Sub-2% inflation and low market-based inflation compensation align with a flatter Phillips curve and anchored expectations (Galí, Gertler, & López-Salido), while the weakness in business investment—often the swing component of the cycle and sensitive to internal funds—echoes financing-constraint findings (Kashyap, Lamont, & Stein, 1994). Overall tone: cautiously positive but risk-aware. sentiment score = 0.20
